Download pre-built backbones or published datasets

Source: R/download.R
taxify_download.Rd

Downloads pre-built .vtr files from GitHub Releases using the taxify manifest. This needs no build tools and does not require taxifydb; it is the fast path taxify() uses internally on first use. Call it directly to pre-fetch backbones and enrichment datasets before an offline session. No prompts are shown, so calling this function is consent.

Usage

taxify_download(
  name = "wfo",
  kind = c("backbone", "enrichment"),
  version = "latest",
  content_id = NULL,
  force = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

name

Character. One or more names from list_backbones() or list_enrichments(), according to kind. With kind = "backbone", "register" resolves the genus register and its coverage table.

kind

Character. "backbone" (default) or "enrichment". Selects the catalogue, including names present in both, such as WCVP.

version

Character. "latest" (default) downloads into the asset's latest/ directory and will be overwritten on future updates. A specific version string (e.g., "2024.01") downloads into a pinned folder retained until explicitly refreshed with force = TRUE.

content_id

Character or NULL (default). The content id of one exact build, the md5 of its .vtr, as recorded by taxify_lock() and by the manifest. Given one, taxify fetches that build from the immutable copy published beside the rolling asset, verifies the bytes hash back to the id, and makes it the active build; the build it replaces is kept under its own content id. Pass one id per name, or one shared by all of them.

force

Logical. Re-download an existing version when TRUE. Default FALSE. An exact content_id identifies immutable bytes.

verbose

Logical. Default TRUE.

Value

Invisibly, a character vector of file paths, named by name and in the requested order. "register" returns the genus-register path after resolving both the register and its coverage table.

Details

If no pre-built .vtr is available for a backbone, it falls back to building from source via taxify_build() (which requires taxifydb).

See also

taxify_build() to build a backbone from source via taxifydb, list_enrichments() for published datasets, taxify_store() for the builds already on disk.

Other Backbone data and cache: lookup_genus(), taxify_build(), taxify_clean(), taxify_clear_cache(), taxify_data_dir(), taxify_example_data(), taxify_load_register(), taxify_lock(), taxify_refresh_manifest(), taxify_register_coverage(), taxify_restore(), taxify_store()

Examples

old <- options(taxify.data_dir = taxify_example_data(),
               taxify.offline = TRUE)
path <- taxify_download("register", verbose = FALSE)
file.exists(path)
#> [1] TRUE
options(old)
